messages:
Jordana: Heads-up — we're seeing a tail-latency regression on canary after today's merge (commit 0f3a2b8). Short-chat INT8 profiles (16 seq / bs4) show ~30-40% P95 increase. I've paused rollout on canary-1 and canary-3 :warning:

Alan: Can you paste the perf snapshot? Is it CPU, GPU, or NVLink?

Jordana: Quick profiler dump from canary-1 (nvprof + pprof):

```text
Sampler: canary-1 / model: redwood-v1-int8 / payload: chat_short
Requests: 1200
Baseline P95: 18ms -> Canary P95: 24-26ms (+33%)
Top time contributors (avg per request):
 - dequant_kernel: 1.20ms (was 0.55ms)
 - kv_cache_lookup: 0.82ms (unchanged)
 - packer/transpose: 0.62ms (was 0.20ms)
 - kernel_select: 0.48ms (new path overhead)
GPU kernels:
 - packer_transpose_int8 (launched more often due to recompile) 34%
 - attention_fwd_int8 18%
```

Sam: That's... packer/transpose jumping up is suspicious. Any trace indicating kernel re-compiles or cache misses?

Jordana: Yes, ptx compile counts increased ~3x around the same time window. nvtx traces show micro-batching decisions flipping between batch-size bins causing the kernel selector to re-evaluate shapes.

Lina: I think this links to the batching hysteresis change in PR #3419 — we reduced hysteresis so small seq-length fluctuations could change the micro-batch bin.

Priya: @Sam @Lina can we bisect to commit? I started a local bisect, it points at 0f3a2b8 (selector + hysteresis tweak). Confirming...

Sam: Thx — I ran `git bisect` on the staging image; repro is deterministic with chat_short. Bisect result: first bad commit 0f3a2b8 "kernel selector: prefer int8 path with dynamic bins". :mag:

Jordana: Root cause hypothesis: batcher hysteresis too tight -> frequent bin switching -> kernel selector compiles/transitions packer layout more often -> packer/transpose path dominates due to suboptimal kernel choice for short sequences. Also dequant_kernel increase comes from an extra dequant fallback codepath added for fallthrough cases.

Lina: Workarounds: 1) bump hysteresis thresholds back, 2) avoid recompile by keying kernels on physical layout + pad to fixed tile for short sequences, 3) revert the dequant fallback until we stabilize.

Sam: I pushed a hotfix branch that reverts the hysteresis tweak and pins the int8 kernel selection to the old rule for seq<=32. PR: https://github.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3437

Priya: Can we run a perf job for chat_short (ci-perf/chat_short_16_4) across canaries before merging? Also add nvtx counters to the CI baseline.

Jordana: Yes — I've queued a CI perf run and held rollout. Deploy bot, please apply hold to release-2026-03-18 canaries.

deploy-bot: rollouts/hold applied to canary-1, canary-3 for release/2026-03-18 by jordana

Alan: Thanks team. After the PR merge we'll rerun the perf harness and if green, unhold and continue canary. Also add perf assertions for ptx-compile-count delta.

Sam: I'll add the assertion and a microbenchmark that exercises the packer path.

Jordana: Filing a follow-up ticket for longer-term: kernel selector needs stability metrics and a test that enforces no new hotpath compiles under small sequence variance. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2112 :memo:

Lina: Great — let's also add a telemetry histogram for "kernel_compile_count" per minute per instance.

Priya: thanks all, holding on further rollouts. :raised_hands:
